title: Tamsin and the Inheritance
premise: Quentin Okonkwo, a night-shift dispatcher for a failing taxi company who moonlights as an unlicensed investigator, is hired by a nervous lawyer to prove that a murder scheduled for the night of the solstice has not yet happened — and to keep it that way. The case hinges on a witness everyone insists died years ago: Tamsin Vey, whose testimony could topple the Harrow family's grip on the city. As Quentin digs through contradictory records, tampered memories, and witnesses who genuinely believe their own false recollections, he realizes someone has been systematically rewriting the past — including pieces of his own. In the end, Quentin finds Tamsin alive in hiding, exposes the memory-doctoring operation run by the Harrows' fixer, and must choose between closing his perfect record and protecting a woman whose survival depends on being forgotten.
about_author: Lena Crane is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing testimonies that never quite matched. She writes mysteries about the gap between what people remember and what actually happened.

chapters.title: The Advance Payment
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Quentin's POV. A rain-soaked night shift; a lawyer named Odile Ferran arrives at the dispatch office with cash and an impossible request: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. Quentin takes the case out of pride and boredom. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Murder Not Yet Committed
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Odile explains: her client stands accused of killing Tamsin Vey, but the trial date is six weeks out and the body was never found. If Tamsin never existed as claimed, the case collapses. Quentin pulls the file and finds it suspiciously clean. Beat: professional thrill tinged with unease.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Quentin interviews three neighbors of the alleged crime scene; all describe Tamsin's death in identical, oddly rehearsed phrasing. He notices they share the same small scar behind the ear. Beat: creeping wrongness beneath ordinary faces.

chapters.title: Night Routes
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, interwoven with dispatch radio chatter. He cross-references taxi logs from the supposed murder night and finds a fare matching Tamsin's description taken to the river district — after her declared time of death. Beat: first real hope, quickly shadowed.

chapters.title: The Harrow Grip
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She warns Quentin off digging into the Harrow family, whose construction empire owns half the city and employs the prosecutor. She reveals her client may be a scapegoat. Beat: fear dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Scar Tissue
chapters.summary: Quentin tracks the shared scar to a defunct clinic, Meridian Rest, where 'voluntary memory therapy' was practiced until its license quietly lapsed. The receptionist remembers nothing — literally. Beat: dawning horror at how deep the erasure goes.

chapters.title: What I Don't Remember
chapters.summary: First-person interlude from Tamsin's hidden POV, unnamed until the final line. She watches news of the trial prep from a rented room, practicing being no one. Beat: quiet defiance and grief for her own erased life.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Smile
chapters.summary: Quentin meets Corwin Ashe, the Harrows' elegant fixer, who offers him triple his fee to drop the case and hints he once met Quentin before. Quentin refuses but can't shake the familiarity. Beat: seduction of corruption, resisted barely.

chapters.title: Gaps in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Quentin audits his own records and finds a two-week hole in his dispatch logs four years ago — the same period Meridian Rest closed. His mother's letters from that month are missing pages. Beat: identity begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A key prosecution witness recants on the stand during pretrial motions, then cannot explain why she ever accused Odile's client. The judge seals the hearing. Beat: hope curdling into suspicion that Odile herself is managed.

chapters.title: River District Ghosts
chapters.summary: Quentin stakes out the ferry terminal where the mystery fare ended. He finds a boarding pass signed 'T. Vey' and a dockworker who remembers a woman who paid him to forget her face. Beat: pursuit sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Session Notes
chapters.summary: Quentin breaks into Meridian Rest's flooded basement archive and steals patient ledgers. Tamsin Vey appears forty-one times — not as a patient, but as the clinic's youngest technician, learning to edit minds. Beat: the victim becomes something more complicated.

chapters.title: Tamsin
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Flashback to her years at Meridian Rest, editing witnesses for Ashe under coercion, until she doctored her own death and vanished. Now she watches Quentin's investigation close in and prepares to run again. Beat: guilt and self-erasure as survival.

chapters.title: The Man Who Met Himself
chapters.summary: Ashe reveals the truth over drinks: Quentin was a Meridian patient after witnessing something he shouldn't have; his perfect closure rate is compensation for a stolen fortnight. Quentin walks out, unsure which memories are his. Beat: devastating identity collapse.

chapters.title: Trial Date Moved Up
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The prosecution accelerates the trial by three weeks — Ashe's move to outrun Quentin. Odile realizes her client will be convicted regardless and confesses she was hired by someone inside the Harrow orbit. Beat: alliances reshuffled, trust fragile.

chapters.title: Two Weeks Missing
chapters.summary: Quentin reconstructs his lost fortnight from physical evidence: a bus ticket, a bruise pattern, a note in his own handwriting reading 'the witness lives.' He understands he found Tamsin once before and chose to forget her to save her. Beat: grief turning into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Quentin and Tamsin finally meet, arranged through the old note. She tests him with details only his erased self would know. They plan to get her testimony recorded before the trial — and before Ashe finds them. Beat: wary, hard-won connection.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Clean
chapters.summary: Ashe's men torch Meridian Rest's remaining records and raid Odile's office. Quentin's apartment is searched; his dispatch logs confiscated. The net closes. Beat: desperation, everything lost except each other.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In a moving taxi — the one place Ashe can't bug — she records her full testimony: the Harrows' use of Meridian Rest to manufacture compliant witnesses across decades. Beat: courage as an act of reclaiming selfhood.

chapters.title: Solstice Night
chapters.summary: Climax. Quentin broadcasts fragments of the recording over the taxi company's radio band while Tamsin surrenders publicly at the courthouse steps, forcing the trial open. Ashe tries to have her committed as mentally unfit; the scarred witnesses begin remembering in open court. Beat: chaos, exposure, sacrifice.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Quentin testifies about his own stolen memories, letting his perfect record shatter to authenticate Tamsin's account. The Harrow heir is indicted; Ashe vanishes, leaving Quentin a single line: 'You were my best work.' Beat: costly vindication.

chapters.title: Dispatch Closed
chapters.summary: Resolution, Quentin's POV. Weeks later, Quentin rebuilds his memory imperfectly, keeps the gaps rather than patching them, and hires Tamsin part-time at the dispatch desk. Some cases don't close; some people choose to remain unfinished. Final beat: peace found in uncertainty.
